knowledge_abstraction.bug_theme: Unaligned storage in BLAS-backed linear algebra operations
knowledge_abstraction.general_principle: Backend libraries may rely on hidden memory alignment assumptions for optimized execution paths; logically valid tensors backed by misaligned storage can violate these assumptions and cause fatal memory access failures.

risk_dimensions.shape: Degenerate or boundary dimensions, such as dimension size 1, that select specialized backend execution paths
risk_dimensions.dtype: Dtypes commonly mapped to BLAS backends, especially float32
risk_dimensions.memory: Logically contiguous tensors backed by misaligned data pointers, for example from slicing larger buffers or applying storage offsets
risk_dimensions.device: CPU backend dispatches to platform-specific BLAS libraries
risk_dimensions.execution_state: Large matrix dimensions or operation shapes that trigger optimized BLAS execution

failure_mechanism.description: BLAS or vectorized backend paths may omit alignment validation before using aligned loads or stores; when a logically contiguous tensor is backed by misaligned memory, the backend can raise a bus error or crash.

input_exploration: Construct tensors that are logically contiguous but are views into larger buffers with controlled storage offsets
Vary alignment offsets, such as modulo 4, 8, or 16, to probe hidden backend alignment assumptions
Test linear algebra operations that share BLAS dispatch, such as matrix-vector, matrix-matrix, and affine transformations
Combine misaligned storage with degenerate leading dimensions and large reduction dimensions
constraint_awareness: Logical contiguity does not imply data pointer alignment
BLAS backends may impose platform-specific alignment constraints
Specialized paths for degenerate dimensions may bypass generic alignment handling
oracle_strategy: Monitor for crash signals such as SIGBUS or SIGSEGV
Compare unaligned executions against aligned reference executions for correctness
Use sanitizers to detect invalid memory access

transferability.reason: Many deep learning framework operations delegate to BLAS or vectorized kernels that assume aligned storage; the risk applies wherever tensor storage can be offset or sliced across APIs.

important_considerations: Focus on storage alignment rather than only tensor shape or dtype
Generate inputs from slices or storage-offset tensors to create misaligned data pointers
Explore related BLAS-backed APIs under the same backend dispatch conditions
generation_strategy: Create generic harness logic that systematically varies storage alignment offsets while preserving logical contiguity, then invokes BLAS-backed APIs and checks for crash signals or mismatches against aligned references.
